extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in television news, media industry professionals, and general news audiences
extracted.subtask_description: A news-piece reporting on a specific journalistic credibility incident (Brian Williams' false Iraq helicopter story), describing the admission, surrounding corrections, and industry implications. Focus is on recounting events and situating them within broader newsroom standards and audience effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not claim events that did not occur; reporting should accurately reflect firsthand experience (the piece notes Williams 'falsely claimed' to have been on a helicopter that was shot down).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborate memories and firsthand accounts before presenting them as fact; avoid conflating separate events. The article cites Williams' own admission: 'I made a mistake in recalling the events 12 years ago.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration with eyewitnesses and contemporaneous accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters should confirm accounts with crew members, eyewitnesses, and contemporaneous reporting (the article contrasts later false retellings with an accurate March 2003 'Dateline' description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contemporaneous reports and direct eyewitness testimony to validate recollections. The veterans and crew members repudiated Williams' later account, showing the need for such checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repeating unverified or embellished narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not retell, promote, or repeat unverified or embellished stories in promotional materials or recent comments (Williams reportedly told and retold the false story in promotional releases and interviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about repeating anecdotes in promos or casual remarks; inaccuracies repeated publicly compound credibility damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source reliability and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify the reliability of information sources (the article notes NBC relied on government-intelligence sources that 'did not give sound facts' in another reporting instance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat claims from intelligence or single-source reports with skepticism until corroborated; failures in source verification have led to retractions (example: incorrect reporting around the Charlie Hebdo suspects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt correction and transparency when inaccurate
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations should correct or update inaccurate reports and be transparent about errors (the article describes NBC updating reports and retracting claims in recent stories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue clear corrections or retractions and explain the cause where appropriate; timely updates mitigate misinformation and public confusion, though the piece notes NBC sometimes updated reports without fully admitting inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and apology
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchors and reporters should acknowledge mistakes and offer apologies when warranted (Williams 'addressed the issue... admitting that he "bungled"' and offered an apology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public acknowledgment and direct apology to affected parties (e.g., veterans) are part of restoring trust after errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with factual record and archival reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistency with the factual record; discrepancies between archival/earlier accurate reports and later recollections undermine credibility (the article contrasts an accurate 2003 Dateline narration with later false recollections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference and rely on archived reports and recordings when reconstructing past events to prevent misremembering or conflating incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize reputational and competitive harm through rigorous standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic errors can provide rivals 'fodder' and affect audience trust and ratings (the article notes competitors could use such mistakes in the struggle for viewers and cites demographic/rating impacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uphold fact-checking and editorial standards not only for ethical reasons but to protect institutional reputation and competitive standing in key audience demographics.
